title: Hearing bebop and swing in New York clubs
summary: Trips to Nick's, Condon's and the Metropole, listening to Coleman Hawkins, Charlie Shavers, Cozy Cole and Roy Eldridge.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you start leaning towards that kind of music, to play bop or hard hop?
Well, as I said earlier, we used to go to New York to go to a certain optician — let me see is it optician or —

No it’s the guy that is a doctor. It’s an optician, isn’t it? Not an optometrist. Not the guy that makes the glasses, no, this is an optician. And as I’d say we’d go, and I was starting to get into listening to the bebop pretty good then. Although we would always go to Nick’s, we’d always go to Condon’s, we went to the Metropole one day and we sat there for eight hours listening to Coleman Hawkins and Charlie Shavers and Mickey Sheen was a great drummer then too. He’s since passed away. And I was in awe. And then they had two bands. The other band was Cozy Cole with Roy Eldridge and certain guys like that, which was amazing too. And I mean I was just staring at this. I said, “man, this is something else.”
